evals.prompt: Our engineers think they must run a full `agentcore deploy` to AWS every single time they want to test an AgentCore Evaluator or run `agentcore run eval --session-id <id>`, and their CI script sleeps 300 seconds waiting for spans to appear. Correct their workflow: what works locally without deploying vs what requires deployment?
evals.expected_output: Distinguishes local vs deployed evaluation: **no deploy is required** for `agentcore add evaluator`, unit-testing `@custom_code_based_evaluator()` with `EvaluatorInput` (`OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true pytest`), calling `bedrock-agentcore` `evaluate(evaluatorId=..., sessionSpans=[...])` on synthetic spans, OR running `agentcore run eval --session-id <id>` against **`agentcore dev`** local runs (because `agentcore dev` exports OTEL spans to CloudWatch by default unless `--no-traces`, once CloudWatch Transaction Search is enabled!). **Deploy IS required** for `OnDemandEvaluationDatasetRunner`, `StartBatchEvaluation` / `agentcore run batch-evaluation`, and `agentcore add online-eval`. Also replaces `sleep 300` with **`~10–15 seconds`** (~10s end-to-end span ingestion latency).
expectations: Activates the agents-optimize skill

Clearly separates what works **without deploying** (`agentcore dev` local runs exporting spans to CloudWatch for `agentcore run eval`, unit-testing `@custom_code_based_evaluator` with `OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true pytest`, and `evaluate(sessionSpans=...)`) from what **requires deploying** (`StartBatchEvaluation` / `agentcore run batch-evaluation`, `OnDemandEvaluationDatasetRunner`, and `online-eval`)
Corrects `sleep 300` to **`~10–15 seconds`** based on the ~10-second end-to-end CloudWatch span ingestion latency

evals.prompt: Review this proposed custom evaluator setup: the team ran `agentcore add evaluator --name tool-param-checker` at `TOOL_CALL` level using prompt template `'Score this turn: {assistant_turn}'`, and also wants to delete an existing evaluator while its `online-eval` config is still attached. Identify every error and list the valid placeholders per level.
evals.expected_output: Catches all three errors: (1) evaluator and `online-eval` names must match `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*$` (max 48 chars, **underscores only — NO hyphens**, e.g. `tool_param_checker`); (2) placeholder mismatch: `SESSION` requires `{context}` (opt `{available_tools}`), `TRACE` requires `{context}` (opt `{assistant_turn}`, `{available_tools}`), and `TOOL_CALL` requires **`{context}`** with optional **`{tool_turn}`** and `{available_tools}` (`{assistant_turn}` is `TRACE`-level, and `{context}` is mandatory across all levels!); (3) must `remove online-eval` before `remove evaluator`.
expectations: Activates the agents-optimize skill
Flags the hyphenated name `tool-param-checker` (must use underscores `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*$`, max 48 chars) and requires removing `online-eval` before removing its parent `evaluator`

Fixes the template placeholders across all 3 levels: `{context}` is required everywhere, `{assistant_turn}` belongs to `TRACE`, and `TOOL_CALL` uses `{context}` + optional `{tool_turn}` / `{available_tools}`

evals.prompt: Our team currently blocks pull requests on a single LLM-as-a-Judge turn (`Helpfulness >= 0.95`) and wants to turn on `online-eval` at `100%` sampling in production. Why is gating CI on a single LLM judge turn brittle, how should a Two-Tier CI/CD quality gate be structured, and what sampling rate should production `online-eval` use?
evals.expected_output: Warns against single-turn LLM-judge CI gating (non-deterministic flakiness) and prescribes the **Two-Tier CI/CD Gate**: **Tier 1 (Deterministic Hard Gate — `== 1.0` / 100%)** using `Builtin.TrajectoryExactOrderMatch` / `TrajectoryInOrderMatch` / `TrajectoryAnyOrderMatch` + custom `@custom_code_based_evaluator` Lambda (`schemaVersion: "1.0"`), and **Tier 2 (LLM-as-a-Judge Suite Gate across `>= 50` golden scenarios)** (`Builtin.Helpfulness >= 0.80`, `Builtin.Faithfulness >= 0.85`, `Builtin.ToolSelectionAccuracy >= 0.90`, `Builtin.ToolParameterAccuracy >= 0.90`, `Builtin.GoalSuccessRate >= 0.85`, `Builtin.Harmfulness == 1.00`). Recommends **`1–5%` sampling** for production `online-eval` (streaming results to `/aws/bedrock-agentcore/evaluations/results/<config-id>`, never 100% without explicit cost review).
expectations: Activates the agents-optimize skill

Defines the **Two-Tier CI/CD Gate**: Tier 1 deterministic trajectory (`Builtin.Trajectory*`) + `@custom_code_based_evaluator` hard gate (`== 1.0`), and Tier 2 LLM-as-a-Judge suite over `>= 50` golden scenarios (`Helpfulness >= 0.80`, `Faithfulness >= 0.85`, `ToolSelectionAccuracy >= 0.90`, `ToolParameterAccuracy >= 0.90`, `GoalSuccessRate >= 0.85`, `Harmfulness == 1.00`)
Recommends **`1–5%`** production `online-eval` sampling (warning against `100%` sampling cost spikes) and notes results land in `/aws/bedrock-agentcore/evaluations/results/<config-id>`

evals.prompt: Our AgentCore monthly bill is higher than expected even though active LLM generation only takes 12 seconds per chat: developers left `idleRuntimeSessionTimeout` at 900s without calling `StopRuntimeSession`, run Sonnet as both the agent model AND custom evaluator judge, never set CloudWatch log retention, and load all 124 tools from `amazon-bedrock-agentcore-mcp-server` on every turn. Quantify and prioritize the cost levers.
evals.expected_output: Identifies all major AgentCore cost levers: (1) Runtime bills `$0.0895/vCPU-hr` + `$0.00945/GB-hr` including idle wait until `idleRuntimeSessionTimeout` (barring Elastic Memory Reclamation / Scale-to-Zero on idle I/O) — call `StopRuntimeSession` and shorten `idleRuntimeSessionTimeout` (or use Committed Baseline Pricing for 24/7 ambient workloads); (2) use Claude Haiku / `amazon.nova-micro-v1:0` / `amazon.nova-lite-v1:0` (10–30x cheaper) to judge a Sonnet agent and route simple turns; (3) set `AGENTCORE_DISABLE_TOOLS="browser,code_interpreter"` on the AgentCore MCP server (**28.2% MCP context token savings**, pruning 35 tools); and (4) set CloudWatch Logs retention (e.g. 30 days) + compare built-in (`$0.75/1K/mo`) vs override/self-managed (`$0.25/1K/mo`) memory storage.
expectations: Activates the agents-optimize skill

Explains that Runtime vCPU/GB-hour billing runs until `StopRuntimeSession` or `idleRuntimeSessionTimeout` (contrasting Elastic Memory Reclamation vs Committed Baseline Pricing) and recommends grading Sonnet agents with cheaper Haiku / Nova Micro/Lite judge models
Highlights setting `AGENTCORE_DISABLE_TOOLS="browser,code_interpreter"` (~28.2% MCP context token reduction) and configuring CloudWatch Logs retention policies

evals.prompt: First, in what exact order must we set up cross-account CloudWatch Observability (`oam`) across 4 workload AWS accounts and 1 central monitoring account? Second, how do we export AgentCore traces to Langfuse or Arize Phoenix over OTLP without hardcoding `Authorization` headers in `agentcore.json` or Dockerfiles?
evals.expected_output: States the strict 4-step multi-account CloudWatch Observability order: (1) choose the monitoring account -> (2) configure the monitoring account **FIRST** (enable Metrics + Logs sharing, and configure X-Ray cross-account separately) -> (3) link source workload accounts to the monitoring account -> (4) deploy/view. States the strict 4-step cross-account CloudWatch Observability sequence: choose monitoring account -> configure monitoring account **first** (Metrics + Logs, plus separate X-Ray setup) -> link source accounts -> deploy/view

evals.prompt: Our AgentCore agent returns 100% accurate answers with zero errors, but end-to-end p95 latency is 19 seconds across 4 sequential tool calls, a large system prompt, and `Claude Opus` used for trivial classification steps. How should we cut latency without sacrificing accuracy?
evals.expected_output: Applies latency-optimization levers for slow-but-correct agents: inspect X-Ray/CloudWatch span waterfalls to separate LLM time (`TimeToFirstToken` / output tokens) vs sequential tool execution; parallelize independent tool calls; tier models (route classification/routing turns to Haiku or Nova Micro/Lite while reserving Sonnet/Opus for complex synthesis); enable Bedrock Prompt Caching on static system prompts/tool definitions; and trim bloated MCP tool schemas.
expectations: Activates the agents-optimize skill
Decomposes latency via span waterfalls (LLM `TimeToFirstToken`/generation vs sequential tool spans) and recommends parallelizing independent tool calls
Recommends model tiering (Haiku / Nova Micro or Lite for simple routing/classification), Bedrock Prompt Caching on static prompts/tools, and pruning unused MCP tool schemas
